- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecasted drop magnitude.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to avoid excessive sell-off.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > +1.0) and price is trending up, model tends to overestimate continuation — slightly dampen upward momentum in later periods.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in early 30-day horizon — adjust downward bias if recent price is above 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +1.5 to -1.5 in 3-5 days), model reacts too slowly — anticipate reversal and adjust forecast 3-5 days ahead.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model often overfits recent noise — use 10-day smoothing or ignore sentiment if volatility is low.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window — apply bias correction for first 7-10 days if sentiment is volatile or price is trending.
- If sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often misreads sentiment — treat as “false signal” and reduce forecasted decline.
